questions.q: How old was Al-Arqam bin Abi Al-Arqam when his house became the headquarters?
questions.explain: His house was sheltered in the Banu Makhzum area.

questions.q: Who taught the Quran to Fatimah bint Al-Khattab and Said?
questions.explain: Khabbab taught them as part of a group of mentors.

questions.q: What was the Prophet's SAW instruction to the companions in the early phase about answering wrongdoing?
options: Be patient and do not retaliate physically
questions.explain: Even with strength, the companions were not allowed to retaliate.

questions.q: What was the focus of the 13 years in Makkah?
options: Tawhid, Paradise, Hell, character and justice
questions.explain: Build the foundation of faith before the rulings.

options: Relationships and mentors that help people grow
questions.explain: A mentor who invests in a relationship can change a life.

questions.q: What did the Prophet SAW build in his companions more than talent?
questions.explain: He also made use of each one's strengths.

questions.q: The early followers came from only one class and one tribe.
questions.explain: False. They came from many statuses, tribes and nations.

questions.q: Change happens gradually, from the individual up to the state.
questions.explain: True. A gradual process is a universal law.

questions.q: Put these events in the right order.

items.text: Abu Bakr brings five key companions
The Yemeni man is asked to go home and wait

questions.explain: Abu Bakr brought five companions, the Yemeni was asked to wait, mentors taught, Sa'd struck, and Dar al-Arqam was chosen.

questions.q: Match each term with its meaning.

right.text: The headquarters house and first school of Islam
One who embraced Islam but does not register or show it

questions.explain: Da'wah fardiyyah is individual da'wah, a silent believer does not show it, tawakkul is reliance on Allah, and Dar al-Arqam was the headquarters.
